source: (Could it be... they're loyal to another above me?)
I'll ask Bernardo to interrogate them shortly. Thank you for your vigilance, Ophelia.
I saw Lady Rosencrantz and Guildenstern acting in a most peculiar way. Could they be the spies you're looking for?
Although they are outsiders to Elsinore, they have been long-time friends of Hamlet's. And they appear to have little interest in Danish affairs.
Or any affairs, anywhere, for that matter.
I'll speak to them, at the very least. Thank you for your vigilance, Ophelia.
Do you know why Queen Gertrude might be rummaging through her husband's things in secret?
I don't know what she might be looking for, if that's what you're asking.
But I... understand why she might not want to simply ask him directly.
Let me only say that there are secrets between King Claudius and Queen Gertrude.
I suspect all marriages are prone to a little secrecy here and there, perhaps.
I wouldn't know, never having been wed myself.
Your mother was searching through your uncle's belongings. Do you know what she might have been looking for?
After all I've learned about her other schemes lately, I hardly care anymore.
Proof, perhaps.
You mean of your father's murder?
Yes. But I doubt her loyalties, and I doubt my assessment of those loyalties.
So I shall not speak to her of it.
Of something larger than either of us. But I doubt her loyalties, and I doubt my assessment of those loyalties.
So I shall not speak to her of it, lest I be revealed.
Queen Gertrude was looking through the King's personal belongings. I don't think he knew it was happening.
Well, only seems fair, considering I do that to her all the time. Her private diary is something special!
Is it really wise of you to come out and admit that?
I'm bored to tears. All I do is wait on Gertrude and help her choose her next soiree gown. Where else am I supposed to find fulfillment?
My lady, I saw you looking through the King's personal belongings. I know.
You-- you did?
What were you doing, if you don't mind my asking?
I do mind, in fact.
It was something very personal, Ophelia. Something I'd like my husband and I to keep between us.
But rest assured, it was no threat to anyone. Not even to him.
My lady told me of this. She is searching for something private. Something which was taken.
Her husband promised her their life would be one of openness, of honesty, of communication.
After so many years with Hamlet-- he was so terribly cold to her.
But Claudius lies to her now in just the same way. Is this the fate of all men with a little power?
My lady is a powerful woman in her own right. She has the blood in her to rule empires. Why is she reduced to digging through a man's closet?
I saw the Queen rummaging through your things.
Yes. Bernardo is addressing it anon. What comes of my wife's dealings is none of your business.
You saw my wife? You're certain?
As the day is long, my lord.
How odd. I inquired with my wife directly, assuming she would naturally have been in my chambers. And yet, she denied it.
I'll... have Bernardo speak to her privately. This is... disconcerting.
I saw the Queen rummaging through the King's things in an odd, hurried way.
Yes. We're addressing it anon. The King is aware - fear not.
The Queen is the one who went through his private items?
But... he asked her directly, and she denied it..
Ophelia, this is a very serious allegation. If it's true...
Then it means the Queen has lied to her husband directly.
I must bring her in and ask her some questions, I think. I'll notify the King.
I saw Bernardo sneaking out of the castle in the early morning hours. You were saying, about a spy...?
You saw that? Hah! No, you needn't worry about him.
Then where is he going, my lord?
Nowhere holy or wholesome. That's all you need to know.
But I've nothing to fear from Bernardo. No—him least of all.
I saw Bernardo sneaking out of the castle in the early morning hours.
Yes. Well.
As far as all that, let's simply say it's none of our concern at the moment.
Not unless Bernardo would like to discuss any of it further.
You mean... about Katherine?
Ah. So you've learned already.
I suspect it's been causing him no small amount of anguish.
Luckily, all that will be resolved soon enough. Bernardo and I are planning to leave town.
Please don't tell anyone.
I won't. I'd suspected something like that might happen.
If Katherine ever wants to express herself fully, she's going to need to do it somewhere better. Happier.
Far away from this sad place.
Do you think it'd help Bernardo if someone went and spoke to him about all this?
Perhaps it's worth a try.
You're the most even-keeled among us. If you can't make Bernardo's life easier, no one can.
I do declare, Ophelia. That's the nicest compliment anyone's ever paid me. I shall try to live up to it.
I saw Bernardo sneaking out of the castle in the early morning hours. What do you know?
Ahhhh, feckin' hell! Only that he's up to no good!
He always makes me take 'is post in his place.
Dunno if it's wine, women, or that other 'w' word. What's the one...
...Waltzing? Wealth?
Whortleberries! That's th' one.
You don' know 'em? All the guards collect 'em in the forest. Then they make pies. We love 'em!
Yeh haven't truly lived until you've had a whortleberry pie with a big ol' mug of whortleberry wine!
I'll have to take your word on that one.
Bernardo, I overheard some mention of your business in town.
Well, you know precisely what.
Oh. I suppose I do, don't I? It all makes sense, now.
...It's nothing very interesting. I can assure you of that.
I would give you the details, but it's quite a long and boring story. It is in your best interest that I spare you.
Have you seen the Guard Captain, Bernardo? Perhaps late in the evening?
Yes. That person has amassed quite the name around here. A rare talent.
But I'm afraid that's all I'm able to say on the matter.
I saw my father burning some documents in his room. You were saying, about a spy...?
Documents? Of what origin?
No... Hrm. It matters not. Whatever he has to hide... all roads must be pursued.
I'll have Bernardo bring your father in for a conversation immediately.
Yes, Bernardo made his treachery clear. I'm thankful that you caught him in the act.
Hopefully some time in a cell will give him a better understanding of his position.
Father, I know you were burning some secretive documents in your room. Can you explain why?
I expected never to speak of them again. And now, I won't.
Those horrid notes are gone forever. And good riddance.
Love, please don't tell anyone about what you saw. Please. It could mean my head.
(Ah. Right. He hasn't burned them yet in this world.)
I don't know what you mean, my love. Don't worry your head over it.
I saw my father burning some documents in his room. The King was saying earlier, about a spy...?
In and of itself, that's not troubling, but I'd like to see him about it regardless.
I'll bring him in for questioning immediately. Thank you for your attentiveness, Ophelia.
Laertes, I saw Father burning something in his chambers late at night. Notes of some sort. Do you know what they were?
I don't.
But do you not trust Father to know what is right in these matters?
I do, but-- I also think those notes contain something important.
If you were to describe what you saw to the wrong people, it would put Father-- and both of us-- in grave danger.
I understand you're curious, Ophelia. But family comes first. Whatever Father was doing, I'm certain he was correct to do so.
What if you bring down suspicion upon him in this climate, and it turns out to have been nothing much at all? Won't you feel silly then?
Bernardo would like to meet with you privately. Could you report to him, please?
This is very sudden... are you certain, my lady? I-if it is your request, of course...
T...this is an insult! How dare he waste my time!
I'm going to give him a piece of my mind.
Ha. Yes, Ophelia, I'll play along.
Come to think of it, I did see something strange. I'll tell him of it.
If he insists. Whatever can he want from me now?
O-of course, at once! I must wonder... why he didn't come to me himself? Oh, bother it, never mind...
Well, of course. I wonder what he's so keen about?
Oh, 'sblood, what have I done now? Mus' be somethin' worth scoldin' me for...
Hah! I no longer take orders from you.
Charming... but I don't answer to you any more, love.
If the good Guard Captain wishes it, then so may it be, of course. Hee hee!
Really? The Guard Captain and I already spoke earlier today.
I think he's heard all he needs to from me today.
Of course. Did he say what it was about?—Ah, I suppose it matters little. I'll see him shortly.
Oh, goodness. Whatever have I done now?
Yes, of course, I'll find him when I'm able.
We've already met him. Guilda dragged me along after you told her the same thing.
We've already met him. Don't you remember? We went to prison.
I think we've been questioned quite enough.
Tell him I didn't steal it! I was only, ahem, borrowing it indefinitely!
Steal what?
Oh, so this isn't about any of the things I've pilfered?
Guilda, you've only been in Elsinore for a little while. How many things did you borrow indefinitely?
Guilda, you haven't even reached the castle yet. How many things did you borrow indefinitely?
Hmm. I so hate doing sums in my head. Let's not worry about the precise numbers here.
Regardless, I shall meet with Bernardo whenever I can pencil the good Guard Captain into my busy schedule!
Ummm... no, thank you.
I already met with him once, with Rosey. I've done my part!
I even went to jail! Absolutely <i>no interest<i> in doing that again.
Horatio, do you know about Bernardo's performance career?
...As Katherine, I mean. Bernardo plays a woman in town performances.
Oh, of course.
Isn't she just fantastic? I caught a show last week.
How could you already know about it?
Honestly, Ophelia, I'm mildly offended you even have to ask. I adore the arts. And Elsinore is where culture goes to die.
